translator.method: LLM translator subagent; no MT service referenced

auditors.model_provenance: Harness model header at run start read 'Model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5'. Mid-run the harness announced four sequential provider-quota fallbacks (anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5, openai/gpt-6-astra, kimi/k3.1-pro, then radient/auto) and its current header line reads 'You are now running as radient/auto'. radient/auto is therefore the model executing the final analysis and writing these receipts; the earlier reading in this run was performed under anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 before the first switch. Where one model must be named it is radient/auto, per the last header the harness issued - not a guess.

model_fallback.note: Four provider-quota switches were announced by the harness during this run; reason given each time: 'provider failure: quota'. The linguistic judgement in these receipts is the delegated run's, but it spans those models, which is why the chain is recorded rather than a single name.

independence: Independent auditor (agent role i18n-auditor; delegated subagent of the parent's run teambridge-notavail-merge-audit-tbm-20261029). It authored none of the translated strings: the not_available values were delivered by i18n-translator job 64be94d56ced (per the prior notavail receipts) and this run verified they are byte-identical to the bytes those receipts audited. No finding reached blocker/major, so this run edited no catalogue at all: every target sha256 here names the unmodified merged working-tree bytes. It wrote only its own receipts and evidence records; it did not commit, push, merge, or touch i18n/ledger.json.

inherited_byte_identical.note: Proof re-derived here, not taken on trust: removing the single line whose stripped form starts with "ui.teamBridge.thread.not_available" from the merged src/i18n/catalogues/es/ui.teamBridge.json and sha256-ing the remainder gives efdc4a0c79f5e672e0e9e124d1b5d53ef3539980a824faa557ab0b1f28a5f974, byte-identical to `git show origin/main:src/i18n/catalogues/es/ui.teamBridge.json` (sha256 efdc4a0c79f5e672e0e9e124d1b5d53ef3539980a824faa557ab0b1f28a5f974) - which is the target_sha256 this ledger row already records (efdc4a0c79f5e672e0e9e124d1b5d53ef3539980a824faa557ab0b1f28a5f974). A difflib unified diff of origin/main against the merged file reports exactly 1 added line and 0 removed, so main's audited bytes are inherited intact and only the new key is new.

scope.english_change: en adds only thread.not_available (value + context note); no other en key changed.

notes: tú register (es guide). 'No tienes acceso' states access, never existence; 'miembro' and 'archivado' match the namespace's member.count and the archive copy; 'Puede que … o que …' offers both reasons and asserts neither. 88 chars vs en 98.
limitations: No rendered evidence: this role has no browser tool and the host is source-only, so fit is judged by character and cell count, not a rendered frame - no maxCells is declared for this key in the en sidecar. fr (117 chars, +19%) and vi (112, +14%) are the two a rendered check should look at first. ur was checked at the code-point level only (no bidi controls, correct Urdu stops, no Latin run); there is no FriBidi or terminal render. Translator provenance (job 64be94d56ced) is inherited from the prior receipts rather than re-verified - what this run did verify is that the delivered strings are byte-identical to those audited. This run is a delegated subagent with no session id of its own, so the instance id is the parent's; and the model changed mid-run under provider quota (see model_provenance), so the judgement spans more than one model. i18n/ledger.json is itself unmerged (UU) at this merge: the working-tree copy read here takes main's rows (c6f6f47ef39d-r2-* with main's target bytes), while the branch side of the conflict names the b393dc8cd01c-notavail-* receipts against the pre-merge branch bytes, so previous_receipt/previous_target_sha256 follow the working tree and the main side - resolving the conflict the other way would change what 'previous' means, not the bytes audited.
